Short technical summary from the runtime side (initial triage):
- Observation window: spike began 08:38 PDT; sustained until our revert actions at 09:05.
- Error profile: 5xx rate peaked at ~2.8% (up from baseline 0.03%).
- Latency: p50 ~350ms (baseline), p99 jumped to 1.9s.
- Correlation: coincident with a canary rollout of hydra-2.3-quant (kernel selection path changed for certain seq-len distributions). We observed cache warming anomalies and increased KV cache misses for session affinity flows.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:05–09:35):
1) Reverted hydra-2.3-quant canary to hydra-2.1-stable across affected clusters.
2) Forced warm pool spin-up for high-concurrency routes and throttled per-client concurrency to reduce head-of-line blocking.
3) Added a temporary routing rule to divert 15% of traffic to hydra-2.1 to validate stability.

Current status: error rate down to ~0.25% and p99 back to ~420ms for the routes we verified. Full rollback verification in progress; ETA for broad baseline recovery: ~45 minutes.

Attachments: runbook patch with quick revert steps.

-David

What happened (high level):

- Impact window on Elara production: ~08:38–09:05 PDT on May 27. Peak checkout failures; estimated conversion impact ~18% during peak.

What we did:
- Immediate rollback of the canary, throttled concurrency, and spun warm pools. Temporary routing to hydra-2.1-stable validated recovery.
- Error rate and p99 latency reduced to near-baseline within ~45 minutes of mitigation.

Customer ask / open items:
- Can you confirm whether your downstream retried requests recovered as expected after 09:15 PDT?
